Native Adventure item/tool/instrument naming source reconstruction

The configured Windows images are Steam PE:6a70a6d9:02711000 and classic
PE:6a70b91c:0270a000. Coordinates in prose are Steam RVAs unless paired
explicitly. native-functions.tsv records exact complete method extents in
both images; chained PE unwind continuations are included. Selector tables
after the code are data, preserved in native-selectors.tsv.

These are offline source materials, not game observations. No native method
is invoked. The Steam full instrument writer source is reused from
../item-description-sources.tsv instead of copied wholesale. The classic
writer is preserved in full as classic-instrument-raw-writer.asm. All writer
conditional edges, literals, call operands, NAME field sequences and bounded
selector entries in both images are in this directory's native-*.tsv files.
The compact steam-percussion-tool-writer.asm preserves the actual complete
percussion name production region around the screenshot noun.

Actual naming route, including the screenshot menu:

  adventure_environment_take_from_pack_animalst.name(out)
    Steam 8932c0; classic 890b40
    if option.item at +28 is null: no caption construction
    out = "Get "
    append complete_item_designation(item, mode=0, article=-1)
      Steam call 89333e -> c65450; classic 890bbe -> c62490
    derive item location from item flags, item/unit container references,
      specific references, or item's direct position
    if option +8 == 0 and pack animal +20 exists:
      append " from " and native unit name/status
    append native cardinal/intercardinal direction from resolved location

  complete_item_designation
    Steam c65450..c65f0a; classic c62490..c62f4a
    preserves native artifact/name branches, named-copy rules, quality,
    wear and improvement wrappers, article mode and stack quantity
    invokes actual item vtable +5e8 title
    full historical graph remains in item-info-title-sources.tsv and
      item-description-sources.tsv; it is not inferred from screenshot words

  Actual RTTI title dispatch:
    item_toolst       type 86  Steam ca39f0; classic ca0a30
    item_weaponst     type 24  Steam ca5bb0; classic ca2bf0
    item_instrumentst type 13  Steam ca5bb0; classic ca2bf0
    all three article-prefix virtuals use c653e0 / classic c62420

The article-prefix method is a separate prefix operation. It appends "the "
for article mode 1. For mode 0, eligible ordinary count-one items receive
"a "; artifacts and other counts do not. Other modes do nothing. It does
not produce the item's noun and does not call complete_item_designation.

Ordinary tool title:

  if native game-mode global is nonzero:
    generic_title(item, out, naming_mode)
  else if item.virtual[90] is false:
    generic_title(item, out, naming_mode)
  else:
    produce the food-storage title using actual stored contents
    native category identities independently select:
      Prepared Food, Seed, Plant, Cheese, Fish, Meat, Spice, Mill,
      Fat, Rendered Fat, Paste, Pressed Material
    another contained-item branch produces complete item designation
    append the tool subtype's singular NAME
    when item material exists, append " (" + material + optional
      ", " + RAW adjective + ")"
      material can include actual named-person possessive and material prefix
      absent material lookup produces "unknown material"
    optional native stored quantity annotation is " <#" + number + ">"

The two full tool methods preserve every category comparison, contained
reference loop, alternate contents branch, material branch, optional
adjective, and quantity branch. Storage grammar belongs to those branches;
the ordinary mallet naming route delegates directly to the generic title.

Generic title:

  collect actual native type, subtype, material type/index, item flags,
    maker race and optional artifact reference
  naming_mode 1 forces count 1
  naming_mode 2 passes count -1
  otherwise read item.virtual[478] quantity
  call shared_item_noun with the complete typed tuple
    Steam ca5d45 -> a82c10; classic ca2d85 -> a7fc90

Shared item noun has all 93 native item-type selector entries, 0..92.
Every selector, jump target and branch is preserved in the paired shared
method ASM and native-selectors.tsv. Equipment, creature/body component,
prepared-food, material and other item branches are existing shared
production families, not alternative literal lists guessed from the image.

TOOL type 86 (Steam selector entry a84432):

  find subtype by its numeric id in the actual itemdef_tool vector
  if found and its RAW ADJECTIVE at +d8 is nonempty:
    append RAW ADJECTIVE + " "
  if the item has a material or material-override mode:
    if the subtype has tool use 10 and its material has native flag 41
       and its live item exists and is not glazed:
      append "unglazed "
    append complete native material qualifier + " "
  if the live item has a valid gem-shape index and the referenced descriptor
      shape has at least one name:
    append its complete first RAW shape name + " "
  if subtype exists:
    append subtype NAME at +68 when count == 1,
      else NAME_PLURAL at +88
  else:
    append "tool" and append "s" when count != 1
  if count > 1: append " [" + count + "]"

There is no test of whether this subtype NAME begins with an invented
instrument name. The subtype is a typed RAW pointer, and its actual string
is consumed directly. A finite recognized bare tool noun can therefore use
the shared material/item composition; requiring an invented-name match is
an extra condition introduced by the translation implementation.

Reachability for the native procedural music-tool definitions:

  The complete paired instrument writers emit no ADJECTIVE, TOOL_USE or
    SHAPE_CATEGORY field. Their material helpers emit only material
    eligibility tokens: Steam eb8ff0 selects THREAD_PLANT_MAT, SILK_MAT or
    LEATHER_MAT; eb9410 selects METAL_MAT, STONE_MAT, WOOD_MAT, CERAMIC_MAT,
    GLASS_MAT, BONE_MAT or SHELL_MAT. They do not supply those missing fields.
  Consequently these generated subtypes have an empty RAW adjective and
    do not satisfy the shared TOOL LIQUID_CONTAINER tool-use condition.
    Steam a84485..a84496 searches subtype.tool_use(+c0) for enum 10; when
    absent, a84499 jumps to a844ea and skips the entire unglazed qualifier.
    Ceramic eligibility by itself does not enable that qualifier.

  item_toolst.getGemShape is a real field getter, not a constant -1:
    vslot +748 -> Steam 28a350 / classic 287f10
      mov eax, DWORD PTR [rcx+100]; ret
    vslot +738 setter -> Steam 28a340 / classic 287f00
      mov DWORD PTR [rcx+100], edx; ret
    The constructor writes shape and face_up to -1 at Steam 28a0b0 /
      classic 287c70. Setting the subtype (Steam c9b830 / classic c98870)
      resolves the itemdef pointer without assigning a shape.
    vslots +730 isGemShapeable and +740 isStoneShapeable both use the
      return-false method Steam 67050 / classic 66fe0.
  The ordinary native shape-assignment method Steam 94bd00 first calls
    +730 at 94be17, then +740 at 94be8f when the first predicate is false.
    With both predicates false it returns without reaching setter 94bf09.
    Generated music-tool creation therefore retains the default shape -1
    along this path and contributes no descriptor-shape prefix.

  Other genuine TOOL shape writes exist but belong to different production
    families. Steam ff6250's divination-tool path requires tool-use enum 24
    at ff7469..ff7498 and a usable subtype.shape_category(+170) entry at
    ff7720..ff775a before setter ff7d27. Native generated music definitions
    supply neither requirement. Steam a8fea0's butcher-product branch reads
    extra_butcher_objectst.shape_id(+28) and invokes setter a917e6 only when
    that authored body-component shape is not -1; this is not an instrument
    crafting product field. These branches show why a field getter must not
    be replaced in the source reconstruction with an unconditional -1.

For a TOOL that does have a live nonnegative shape, the generic noun method
still uses the complete first descriptor_shape.names entry before the RAW
tool NAME. Its grammar is material + descriptor RAW NAME + subtype NAME;
the musical-description shape labels such as bowl-shaped and hourglass are
a different field. Existing descriptor_shape_standard.txt RAW names and
Overlay::load_symbol_shape_forms / translate_symbol_shape provide the
typed descriptor-shape vocabulary. Their presence does not make this
prefix reachable for the native music definitions described above.

INSTRUMENT type 13 (Steam a8435c):

  append material qualifier when present
  find instrument subtype by actual numeric id
  if found: copy singular/plural subtype NAME at +68/+88
  else: use "musical instrument", pluralize for count != 1
  append stack quantity for count > 1

Actual authored RAW source text is retained under raw-sources/ with NAME,
ADJECTIVE and DESCRIPTION field coordinates in raw-name-fields.tsv. The
installed vanilla item_tool and item_weapon definitions do not contain
mallet. The existing Wanderer reaction source mentions Mallet only inside
reaction NAME labels. That text alone does not identify a WEAPON or TOOL
subtype and is not used as item-type evidence.

Native procedural instrument writer:

  Steam ebe8a0..ecc30c; classic eb9810..ec727c
  four requested instrument-family count fields select independent keyboard,
    string, wind and percussion generation loops
  each loop chooses/reuses an invented instrument name, writes generated
    ITEM_TOOL component definitions and ITEM_INSTRUMENT definitions, writes
    stored descriptions, and writes crafting/assembly reaction definitions
  the complete finite component name fields and plural modes are in
    native-piece-fields.tsv
  native-name-productions.tsv preserves each NAME construction's dynamic
    stack-field operands, literal suffixes, and conditional field ordering
  arbitrary authored RAW values and invented instrument names remain data;
    a finite noun inventory is not an enumeration of every complete name

INSTRUMENT_PIECE fields use two different plural contracts:

  STANDARD: separate singular and plural piece names
  ALWAYS_PLURAL: the plural name is also used in the nominal singular slot

Keyboard family finite fields include keyboard/keyboards, console/consoles,
body/bodies, case/cases, chest/chests, strings/strings, bells/bells,
pipes/pipes, pump/pumps and bellows/bellows.

String family finite fields include neck/necks, body/bodies, frame/frames,
yoke/yokes, sound-chest/sound-chests, string/strings, strings/strings,
bow/bows, plectrum/plectra, hammers/hammers and neck bowl/neck bowls.
The hammers component is ALWAYS_PLURAL; it is a different production from
the percussion hammer/hammers selector.

Wind family finite fields include bellows/bellows, blowpipe/blowpipes,
bag/bags, melody pipe/melody pipes, drone pipe/drone pipes,
drone pipes/drone pipes, wind chest/wind chests and pipe/pipes.

Percussion striking-tool selector (Steam ec8099 onward):

  native random branch 0 -> mallets/mallet  ec8105/ec8131
  native random branch 1 -> hammers/hammer ec80d0/ec80fc
  native random branch 2 -> sticks/stick   ec80b0/ec80c7
  corresponding classic literal operands:
    mallets/mallet ec3075/ec30a1
    hammers/hammer ec3040/ec306c
    sticks/stick   ec3020/ec3037
  number of strikers controls the nominal singular string; multi-striker
    forms use the plural label in both name slots
  native-piece-fields.tsv anchors each finite noun selector at its first
    literal operand. That anchor is a branch/source coordinate, not a claim
    that the operand at that address is the singular form.

Percussion body selector:

  membrane branch -> drum/drums
  other branch -> seven native table entries, Steam ec83a6 table ecc2f0:
    bar/bars, chime/chimes, block/blocks, bowl/bowls,
    triangle/triangles, bell/bells, ring/rings
  native count selects the nominal singular field or an ALWAYS_PLURAL field
  other component fields include stand/stands and head/heads,
    with heads/heads in the ALWAYS_PLURAL branch
  drum-shape data separately selects bowl-shaped, tube, barrel, goblet,
    hourglass; these strings are stored description/shape operands rather
    than interchangeable aliases for the piece noun

Critical NAME construction distinction:

  The generated percussion _MALLET tool NAME is NOT a bare mallet string.
  Steam ec9186..ec9228 and classic ec40f6..ec419c write:
    [NAME:{invented instrument name} {nominal striker name}:
          {invented instrument name} {plural striker name}]
    invented name is stack string rbp+3a0
    nominal striker name is rbp+4a0
    plural striker name is rbp+500
  The common TOOL title reader does not require that invented prefix.
  The screenshot's bare "rhyolite mallet" is direct display evidence of
    the bare form; this extraction does not invent a claim that the native
    writer above always creates raw NAME=mallet without a prefix.

Translation scope follows the exact production roles. Native finite
striking-tool nouns and recognized complete material prefixes can be
composed on the ordinary item path. Generic overlapping component nouns
such as bag, bow, bar, block, bowl and ring need their typed/generated
instrument context. They must not be globally reinterpreted as instruments.
The full current instrument-translations.tsv already contains the finite
piece keys from these sources, including bar/block/bowl/ring forms later
in the file. The original translation failure is an unreachable composition
branch, not absence of the mallet noun entry.
